rootCauseOneLine: codex app-server replays the previous turn's token usage on thread/resume and thread/fork; the codex bridge stamps that old Codex turn id with the NEW session's per-session prefix (bt<entropy>-<serial>-), so the server sees a turn it never stored turn/started for and (by design) drops the snapshot with a warn log — on resume the payload is an exact duplicate of what is already stored (log noise only), on fork the parent's inherited context usage is discarded until the fork's first turn.
proposedFix: Keep the server-side orphan drop (it is the correct safety net; buffering would re-create the fork batch-wedging bug). Fix in the codex bridge (plugins/provider-codex/src/bridge/bridge.ts, toCanonicalEvents ~L620): track Codex turn ids this session has emitted turn/started for; for thread/tokenUsage/updated or thread/contextWindowUsage/updated naming any other turn (only resume/fork replays do that), emit the context-window usage thread-scoped ({kind:"thread"} is allowed by the domain scope policy and is what the ACP bridge already does) and drop the token usage (turn-only by policy; duplicate of the persisted snapshot on resume, parent's cumulative total on fork). Prototype diff in the artifacts typechecks and keeps the full codex plugin suite green (165 passed). Optionally add scope.turnId to the server warn line and lower it to info/debug. No wire changes, no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
caveats: Not a visual bug, so no screenshots. The worktree was created at a108fa7ef (origin/main tip) rather than 16ceb3a54; I checked out 16ceb3a54 before the live runs and rebuilt (relevant files are equivalent between the two). The bridge-level repro test needs a small opt-in extension of the test fixture fake-codex-app-server.mjs (diff included) to mirror the real app-server's usage replay on resume; the real behavior is proven separately by the raw codex app-server probe and the live bb runs. Server-log instrumentation (adds scope/data to the warn line) was applied for the second live run only to show which turn id was dropped; the warning itself reproduces without it. Live runs consumed a handful of tiny codex turns ("Reply only with ok.").
